speaker: Dr. Regolith
lines: Welcome aboard, pilot. I am Dr. Regolith, and today the Moon's south pole is your office.
Why the pole? Some craters there are permanently shadowed, so cold that water ice survives inside them for billions of years. Ice means water, oxygen and rocket fuel.
Nearby crater rims and ridges can catch long stretches of sunlight, which is ideal for solar power and for keeping a lander warm.
From the pole, Earth hangs low on the horizon. A site with a clear view of it keeps your radio link alive.
Slopes, sunlight, cold and comms all matter. Read the cards, trust the data, and pick your landing site wisely. Choose well, pilot.
